video.title: 25 ChatGPT Hacks You Need to Know in 2026 (Profit, Become a Pro!)

summary: Chris Koerner presents ways to use ChatGPT and other AI tools for research, writing, business brainstorming, and repeatable workflows. He recommends giving AI specific context, refining prompts, and testing ideas with real audience feedback. Business examples include a local market research app, a review-fixing service, and several physical product or service concepts. The video focuses on prompting techniques rather than operating any of those businesses, and it promotes the host’s community, newsletter, and podcast.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office and presenter of the video.

ideas.name: Local review and market gap research app
ideas.one_liner: Use Google Maps and OpenAI to compare local businesses’ reviews and market density across similar cities.
ideas.customer: Not stated; the example is aimed at a prospective founder researching local markets.
ideas.problem: A founder may not know which local industries have poor customer experiences or are underserved.
ideas.offer: An app that finds industries with poor reviews, compares business density and review ratings across comparable cities, and flags potential opportunities.

pricing.notes: The host describes building an app but gives no pricing or sales model.

ideas.delivery: The host suggests using Replit to build an app that pulls Google Maps reviews through the Google Maps API and analyzes them with the OpenAI API. It would identify local industries with poor reviews and compare them with similar cities.

acquisition.how: The transcript gives no way to find paying customers. If sold as software, agents could support inbound marketing and lead qualification, with a human checking demand and positioning.

onboarding.how: A web app could collect a location and industry automatically; a human may need to resolve data or setup issues.

delivery.how: Review collection, analysis, and city comparisons could run automatically, with occasional human checks for data quality and relevance.

billing.how: A subscription payment system could handle recurring billing and receipts automatically.

support.how: Agents could answer common product questions, while a human handles API failures and disputed analysis.

uk_applicability.notes: The research approach can transfer to UK towns and cities, but local market comparisons and review-data handling would need UK-specific setup. The transcript gives only US city examples.

risks: The host does not describe how the app would get permission to use review data or whether the APIs allow the proposed collection and comparison.
A weak city comparison could mistake differences in business mix or review volume for a real market gap.

quotes.text: and then you could have your app in Replet find the top five business industries in your local area that are notorious for having the worst reviews
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Plumbing business in an underserved city
ideas.one_liner: Open a plumbing business in a city where the host’s hypothetical comparison suggests lower competition and poorer customer experiences.
ideas.customer: People in Houston who have a poor experience with plumbers; the specific customer segment is not stated.
ideas.problem: The host’s hypothetical example suggests that Houston has relatively few plumbing businesses and lower average review ratings than Dallas.
ideas.offer: Open a plumbing business in Houston. Services, staffing, and operating model are not stated.
ideas.delivery: A plumbing business would provide local plumbing work. The host gives no details about who performs the work or how it is delivered.
unit_economics_claims: The host gives a hypothetical comparison of plumbing-business density and average review ratings in Dallas and Houston.

acquisition.how: The host does not state a customer acquisition method. Local trust-building and sales would likely need human involvement.

onboarding.how: Agents could collect job details, but a person would need to assess work and arrange service.

delivery.how: Plumbing work takes place in person and must be performed by a human.

billing.how: Software could issue quotes, invoices, and payment reminders, with a person checking job-specific charges.

support.how: Agents could answer routine questions, but a person would need to handle urgent, technical, or safety-related issues.

uk_applicability.notes: A local plumbing business can operate in the UK, but the market comparison is based on US cities and local qualifications, pricing, and customer acquisition would need UK-specific work.

risks: The Dallas and Houston figures are hypothetical examples, not verified market research.
Poor reviews and lower business density do not by themselves prove that customers will choose a new provider.

quotes.text: there's two very very relevant data points that tell me I need to open a plumbing business in Houston because it's half as saturated
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

onboarding.how: An agent could gather business details and review history, with a person confirming the actual problem and scope.

delivery.how: The host does not define the fix. Review analysis and recommendations could be automated, but many likely fixes would require human work.

acquisition_channels.details: The host says the generated blog articles are intended to be SEO-friendly and to rank for selected search terms; he does not describe how a service provider would acquire clients.

ideas.delivery: ChatGPT rewrites customer reviews into keyword-focused blog articles. A human would need to check the content and confirm that it accurately represents customer feedback.

acquisition.how: The transcript gives no client acquisition plan. Agents could help produce educational content and qualify inbound enquiries, with human oversight.

onboarding.how: A form could collect reviews, keywords, and brand guidance automatically; a human should confirm permissions and the brief.

tactics.name: Prompt for strategies and angles
steps: Ask for angles, tactics, and strategy instead of a broad request for facts.
Specify the type of opportunity, audience, or outcome you want the model to explore.
Use the response as a starting point and follow up on promising directions.

quote.text: don't just ask it for facts ask it for angles tactics leverage instead of saying things like What are some good business ideas?
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Give the model reference material
steps: State the audience and desired reading level or style.
Provide examples, images, video, or text that show what you want.
Ask the model what makes a set of examples effective, then reuse those findings in a project.

quote.text: feed it as much reference data as you can whether that's an image a video or just text
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Turn prompts into reusable workflows
steps: Write a prompt that can produce the same kind of result repeatedly.
Save it in a custom GPT or project.
Upload strong examples and ask the model to identify the qualities to reproduce.

quote.text: you're not asking for answers you're asking for systems because the quality of your questions is the ceiling of your output
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Test content angles with audience polls
steps: Ask ChatGPT for eight marketing angles.
Run polls with four options at a time, asking which YouTube title people would click.
Let each poll run for about 30 minutes, then take one or two winners into a final bracket-style poll.
Use the winning angle to write the title, thumbnail, newsletter, or post.

quote.text: i will take four of the eight marketing angles post them as a poll and say Which YouTube title would you click on?
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use customer reviews as research and content
steps: Collect customer reviews for a business or niche.
Use the review language to identify customer problems and search terms.
Turn suitable review themes into keyword-focused content or a specific service offer.
Check the facts and obtain any needed permissions before publishing customer material.

quote.text: you could just go to Google Maps you can just start searching around for businesses you could find any old business you can copy and paste all their reviews and then plug that into your chat as a source of reference
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Compare local markets before choosing a business
steps: Identify industries with poor reviews in a local area.
Choose comparable cities and compare business density and average review ratings.
Treat differences as leads for further validation, not proof that a new business will succeed.

quote.text: there's two very very relevant data points that tell me I need to open a plumbing business in Houston because it's half as saturated
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Refine answers across models
steps: Ask the same question in several language models.
Compare the responses and choose the one with the most useful answer.
Show another model that response, explain what works or is missing, and ask it to improve.

quote.text: take the same prompt the same question ask it to all four but instead of inserting that little sentence about jealousy don't even reference the other LLM just reference what the other LLM is saying and then ask it to do better
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

evidence_quality.rationale: This is a host-led roundup of prompting tips, with some first-hand examples but little verifiable business performance evidence. The local market figures are hypothetical, and several ideas are only prompts with no described offer or operating results.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: The host promotes TK Owners, his newsletter, and his podcast during the video.
